section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The OS_ReadSysInfo SWI has been extended and modified since the calls documented in the PRMs. The full list of OS_ReadSysInfo reason codes currently supported is :

value-table.value: Read configured screen size
Read configured mode, monitor type and sync
Read chip presence and unique machine ID
Read features mask for 82C710-compatible chip family
Read machine ethernet address
Read raw unique ID
Read kernel values
Read last abort details
Read platform class
Read ROM information
Read Operating System version
Read debug information

use.p: This SWI no longer returns any configured screen size details. The screen size is managed entirely at the discretion of the video driver modules. Originally this SWI returned the size of the configured screen memory in bytes.

swi-definition.name: OS_ReadSysInfo
swi-definition.description: Read configured mode, monitor type and sync

exit.register-use: Configured mode
Configured monitor type
Configured sync

use.p: This SWI reads the configured mode, monitor type and sync type as previously. Whilst the values are configurable, it is recommended that they be set to Auto except where this is a problem. The automatic detection of monitor type will be performed by the video hardware as necessary.

use.p: This SWI is used to read information on the hardware used within the system. In many cases this will be determined by the hardware drivers rather than the Kernel, and it is therefore prudent to interrogate the specific hardware driver modules rather than the Kernel. The Kernel restricts itself, in general, to those tasks which it is vital to perform for system start up and management. The operation of the hardware devices outside of this is the domain of the hardware drivers and correspondingly many of the fields may appear as 'undefined'.

use.p: This SWI has been updated to reflect the modern usage of the hardware IO chips used in RISC OS systems to date. It will return 0 in all fields for non-82C710-compatible chipsets. See PRM 1-723 and PRM 5a-221 for more details.

exit.register-use: Ethernet MAC address word 0, or 0 if not known
Ethernet MAC address word 1, or 0 if not known

use.p: This SWI is used to read the machine's ethernet address. It should only be used within constrained environments where only a single ethernet network interface is available. This SWI was introduced to allow simpler expansion of systems with only a single network interface. It is recommended that network drivers should only use their own unique MAC address in preference to this value.

exit.register-use: Raw machine ID word 0
Raw machine ID word 1

use.p: This SWI is used to read the raw machine ID as read from the system hardware. No interpretation should be placed upon the value by clients.

entry.register-use: Pointer to list of kernel values to read, or 0 to read a single value
Pointer to block to fill in with values, or (if R1 = 0) the single kernel value to read

exit.register-use: Block at R2 filled in, or (if R1 was 0) the value of the single item

use.p: This SWI can be used to obtain information about the Kernel's internal variables which it chooses to export. The variables are subject to change and may have caveats on their use. They are only expected to be used by components where the operation required is not supported by defined interfaces. In such cases, using the information provided by OS_ReadSysInfo 6 is preferred over using hard-coded values. Using information provided by more structured interfaces which the OS provides is preferred over using OS_ReadSysInfo 6.
The following values are defined. Strictly they are reserved for internal use, but are provided for completeness.

use.p: Any item may return an error, or the value 0 when being read to indicate that it is unavailable.

exit.register-use: Preserved
32-bit PC of last abort
32-bit PSR of last abort
Fault address of last abort

use.p: This SWI returns the details about the last failing abort. The fault address is the same as the 32bit PC for a pre-fetch abort. For a data abort, it contains the address whose access caused the abort. Aborts which are handled by other components may occur, and do not update these details. Such aborts are handled by the interface, or the DynamicArea abort handlers. See the abort trapping and dynamic area documents for more details.

use.p: This SWI is used to read details about the platform upon which the OS is running.

entry.register-use:
Item to return:
OS name Release part number Build date Dealer name User name User address Printable OS description Reserved

exit.register-use: Pointer to requested string or 0 if item is not defined

use.p: This SWI is used to read details about the ROM build and details. It may be used to read additional information about the system in order to provide diagnostics. It is important that privacy concerns be addressed if such information is distributed, particularly if the user name and address fields are to be exported.

exit.register-use: OS version number * 100
Kernel version number * 100

SystemInit version number and system type:
Version number Init type:
RiscPC Reserved
Reserved (0)

use.p: This SWI is used to read the version number of the Operating System and Kernel. In order to differentiate between the OS as a whole and the Kernel itself, this SWI provides a mechanism for reading the version number of both.

The operating system version is contained within the help string for the UtilityModule. This describes the system as a whole. It should be used when checking for the general level of compatibility is required.

The Kernel version has, in the past, only been returned by the return from OS_Byte 0 as part of the error report. This interface defines a mechanism by which the version can be obtained without needing to parse a free-format string.
The SystemInit version number and system type are returned by the initialisation code and indicate the basic loader which is used to enter the Operating System.
The value returned in R3 will be defined in a future version of this call, and should not be interpreted by software.
This SWI call is available from Kernel 9.03.

exit.register-use: Pointer to function for debug character output
Pointer to function for debug character input

use.p: This SWI is used to read the diagnostic functions provided by the SystemInit code in order to debug the system. Usually this is a simple serial I/O stream which is managed by the SystemInit code, although other mechanisms may be employed dependent on hardware. The functions are expected to be called from a privileged mode, although operation in non-privileged modes is at the discretion of the SystemInit code. Both routines expect a small amount of stack to be available.

entry.register-use: Character to write to debug stream

exit.register-use: Corrupted, as is the PSR

use.p: Writes a character to the debug stream. The address of the routine is read with OS_ReadSysInfo 11.

exit.register-use: Character read from debug stream, or -1 if no character available
Corrupted, as is the PSR

use.p: Reads a character from the debug stream. The address of the routine is read with OS_ReadSysInfo 11.
